# Shared by the children below, which run in this order in one R session.
# qqJasp(): the Q-Q plot as JASP draws it (jaspGraphs::plotQQnorm, 95% band, standardized
# residuals). Pass the residuals JASP uses: t-tests scale(y - group mean) or scale(differences),
# ANOVA rstandard(lm(...)).
qqJasp <- function(res) {
  suppressWarnings(print(jaspGraphs::plotQQnorm(res, yName = "Standardized residuals", ablineColor = "darkred",
                                                ablineOrigin = TRUE, identicalAxes = TRUE, ciLevel = 0.95)))
}
# dsjLinks(): data and results of a DSUJ data set on discoverjasp.com.
dsjLinks <- function(name) {
  sprintf(paste("[Data (.jasp)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_data/data/%1$s.jasp) ·",
                "[Results (.jasp)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_data/results/%1$s.jasp) ·",
                "[Results (.html)](https://discoverjasp.com/repository/dsj1_data/html/%1$s.html)"), name)
}

## Bootstrapping (bonus) {.smaller}

Not needed for the exam, but you will meet it in the book (Section 6.10.5) and in JASP

- Treat the sample as the population and draw new samples from it, with replacement
- Compute the statistic in each bootstrap sample (JASP uses 1000 by default)
- The middle 95% of those estimates gives a bootstrap confidence interval
- No need to assume the shape of the sampling distribution
- In JASP mostly a way to get more robust confidence intervals
  - Usually a checkbox "From ... bootstraps"
  - Correlation, linear regression, ANOVA post hoc tests, Descriptives, PROCESS (lecture 23)
- Random resampling, so the numbers differ slightly each time

# Closing

## Recap

- Non-parametric tests are rank-based, which means they are robust to:
  - Non-normality
  - Transformations of the data
  - Outliers

## Recap lecture 18: $t$-test = ANOVA = regression {.smaller}

The same pre- and posttest scores, analyzed in two ways

- Ignoring participants, independent $t$-test = one-way ANOVA = regression
- Accounting for participants, paired $t$-test = RM ANOVA = ANOVA or regression with `id`
- `y`, `id` and `time-point`, long format (one row per measurement)
- `pre-test`, `post-test` and `diff-scores`, wide format (one row per participant)

[Data (.csv)](https://johnnydoorn.github.io/teaching-statistics/datasets/2026/equivalence-anova-t-test.csv) · [Results (.jasp)](https://johnnydoorn.github.io/teaching-statistics/datasets/equivalenceBetweenAllTests.jasp) · [Results (.html)](https://johnnydoorn.github.io/teaching-statistics/datasets/equivalenceBetweenAllTests.html)

## Exam note: assumptions per analysis {.smaller}

- All analyses below assume normal residuals (Q-Q plot with confidence band)
- Violations (normality, variances, sphericity) mess up Type I/II error rates
- How to assess them (next slides)

::: {style="font-size: 75%;"}
| Analysis | Also assumes | If unequal variances or no sphericity | If non-normal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paired $t$-test | – | – | Wilcoxon signed-rank |
| Independent $t$-test | Equal variances | Welch $t$ | Mann-Whitney |
| One-way ANOVA | Equal variances | Welch $F$ | Kruskal-Wallis |
| Factorial ANOVA | Equal variances | – | – |
| ANCOVA | Equal variances, independent covariate, equal slopes | – | – |
| RM ANOVA | Sphericity (3+ levels) | Greenhouse-Geisser | Friedman (one-way only) |
| Mixed ANOVA | Equal variances, sphericity | Greenhouse-Geisser | – |
:::
